xref.title: Band Name Origin ("All My Sons")
xref.body: The band's name is derived from Arthur Miller's 1947 play, "All My Sons," which is based on a true story. The play tells of an Ohio man who knowingly approved defective aircraft engines for use in World War II, leading to the deaths of 21 pilots. "This play is called All My Sons from 1947. And it's based on a true story about a man also from Ohio who conspired with the army to approve faulty and defective aircraft engines for use in combat in World War II. And as a result of this bad equipment, 21 pilots died."

xref.title: Inspiration from Arthur Miller
xref.body: The song "Somewhere There's An Angel" by The Thirst in Revival was directly inspired by the classic Arthur Miller play "The Crucible." The composition and writing process for this track took Dan O'Donnell two years to complete, reflecting a deep engagement with its thematic origins. "Dan says that this song was inspired by the classic Arthur Miller play The Crucible and it took him two years to write."
